About Event

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.
READY TO BUILD?

If you're excited about the future of AI, agents and scientific discovery, we'll see you there...
We will close applications on Thursday, 30th of July, 12 PM PST. Spots will be confirmed on Friday, 31st of July.
WHO SHOULD ATTEND
People with the questions: scientists of all stripes. Wet lab, computational, clinical, industry. Biology, biochemistry, biophysics, chemistry, structural. Anyone with a real problem, ideally a real dataset, and the judgment to tell right from wrong results.
People who build for a living: ML engineers, software developers, and agent builders who can take a half-formed scientific problem and ship something that runs by Sunday.
No prior AI expertise required. Participants are welcome at all levels.

Tracks
Track A: Build an AI Scientist
Build an AI agent that can carry out a defined scientific or drug-development workflow from start to finish. It should gather evidence, use relevant tools or databases, generate and test hypotheses, produce a structured output, and make its reasoning easy to inspect. This could mean reasoning over experimental data, scientific literature, or learned representations like protein embeddings. Examples include a virtual FDA reviewer, toxicology agent, clinical trial designer, experimental planning agent, or a protein-discovery agent that generates and tests hypotheses over protein embeddings and structural features.
Track B: Build a Dataset or Meta-Analysis

What have you always wanted the literature to tell you, but could never read fast enough to find out? Draft the queries, run them across thousands of papers, sharpen and re-run until the results hold the specific pieces you care about. Then the real work: find the pattern in what you assembled that no single paper could show you, and demo that.
Track C: Build the Biological Design

Assemble a pipeline that designs biology to a spec you choose, from a single protein up to a multi-gene system. You set the constraints; the models generate candidates and evolve them toward something that could hold up in a real cell. Could the literature reveal the most promising design space for a generative model to explore? What you demo is the new biological design you made — the sequence or system that didn't exist before you built it.
Or come with a different project of your own.
Prizes will be awarded.

FAQs
Do I need a biology background or an AI background to participate?

No. We're looking for engineers with no life sciences experience as well as individuals who are in life sciences. One is helpful, but you don’t need both. The best teams usually pair technical builders with someone who knows the science.
Do I need a team before applying?
No. You can apply as a team, but you don’t have to. You can apply solo, and you'll meet potential teammates at the kickoff event.
What will I have access to during the hackathon?

Free Paperclip API access, access to Proto , Claude API credits, and compute and credits from our sponsors.
Is there a cost to attend?
The event is free to attend. Food, drinks, and compute are covered .
What happens to what I build afterward?

You keep it. Teams are free to open-source, continue building, or spin their project into something bigger.

About Event

MakerMods Physical AI Hacks 🤖
This is the best Physical AI hackathon you've been looking for.

Join MakerMods and Dream Labs on November 7–8 at Founders Inc. in San Francisco for a weekend of building physical AI: robots that act on the world, agents that coordinate those actions, and applications that bring the two together.
We’re bringing bimanual 6-axis robot arms, Dream Labs’ Dream-1, and a target of 200 builders into one space. Bring your ideas, your teammates, and a willingness to debug something that can actually move.
Brough to you by:
MakerMods
MakerMods is a full-stack robotics company making Physical AI accessible to everyone. We build affordable robot hardware and software that lets people teach robots to do physical tasks—from makers experimenting at home to researchers building the next generation of robot intelligence. Built for makers, by makers.
Dream Labs
Dream Labs is bringing “everyday capabilities to everyday robots.” Its robot brain, Dream-1, is built to work across different robots, tasks, and environments. Through the Dream API, developers can turn camera observations and task instructions into robot actions, and adapt the model with their own demonstrations.
The Challege:
Two ways to build
🏁 Hill Climb
One challenge. One leaderboard.
Take on a shared, long horizon Physical AI tasks using our Metal Arm stations.
Your team's rank is based only on your eval score.
No pitching. No larping. It's all skill based.
You’ll collect demonstrations and fine-tune the lastest SOTA World Action Model by Dream Labs: Dream-1. Then your team builds the harness around the model: deciding what happens next, checking whether an action worked, and recovering when it didn’t.
The same Dream-1 model can produce very different results depending on the fine-tuning data and the harness you build around it.
Can your robot finish the task? Can it recover from a failed attempt? Can you push your score higher before the deadline?
Scores come from task performance against published rules. Leading teams will make scored attempts live on stage while the competition continues at the other stations.
The full challenge and scoring rules will be shared before the event.
💡 Creative Applications (Track 2) What would you build if your agent had robot arms?
Build an application around Dream-1 and our Maker Arm stations.
Connect robot actions to voice, agents, human input, and everyday tools. Make something useful, surprising, playful—or something nobody in the room would have thought to try.
Some directions to explore:
A voice-controlled assistant that asks for help when it gets stuck.

A robot workflow triggered by a calendar event or a message.

An interactive experience where people and robots solve something together.

A physical tool your software agent can call to get a real-world job done.

Book robot time, bring your own props or work creatively with the materials available, and film your project in action.
Three finalists will pitch on stage with their demo videos. A judging panel will select first, second, and third place.
Creative awards are judged separately from the hill-climb leaderboard, with the rubric published beforehand.
Who should join?
Robot-learning researchers. ML engineers. Agent builders. Hardware hackers. Students. Designers with an idea that needs to exist outside a screen.
You don’t need to arrive as a robotics expert. Teams will need different strengths: collecting demonstrations, building agents, integrating tools, designing interactions, and making the whole stack work. Workshops from MakerMods, Dream Labs and more sponsors will help you get familiar with frontier Physical AI robotics hardware and world action models.
If you’ve been looking for a reason to try physical AI on real hardware, this is it.
What to expect
Shared access to real bimanual robot stations.

Dream-1 access for building and running your projects.

An opening setup workshop to help teams get started.

A weekend of building alongside people working across robotics and AI.

Live robot attempts, creative project pitches, and awards across both tracks.

Robot time will be booked and shared across teams. Plan to use time away from the arms for coding, reviewing data, and improving your application.
The details
📍 Founders Inc., San Francisco 📅 November 7–8, 2026 👥 Teams of 3–6; around five is ideal 🤝 Apply with a team or apply solo and meet other builders
Bring your laptop and charger. For creative projects, you’re welcome to bring props; we’ll share setup and hardware guidance before the event.
The detailed schedule, station-booking process, challenge rules, prize announcements, and confirmed partners will follow.
Ready to build?
Apply to join MakerMods Physical AI Hacks.
Bring an idea. Leave with a robot doing something you built.

🛑 Learning was never text-only. Kids read out loud, scribble on worksheets, point at diagrams, and think with their hands. Now AI can hear, see, and watch too.

Multi-Modal AI for Education
A text box only catches what a student types. A great teacher notices much more: the pause before a hard word, the crossed-out step in a math problem, the moment a class goes quiet. Multi-modal AI can finally pick up those signals. Voice, handwriting, images, and video can all become part of how we teach.

🎙️ Track 1 · Voice & Audio Tutors
Tutors that listen as well as talk. Hear a student read or think out loud, catch exactly where they get stuck, and respond like a patient coach.
Ideas: a read-aloud fluency coach that hears which words a kid stumbles on · a think-aloud math tutor that spots the misconception in a spoken explanation · a speaking partner for language learners · voice-first learning for students with dyslexia or low vision
✍️ Track 2 · Vision, Handwriting & Documents
Learning happens on paper. Build AI that reads handwritten work, worksheets, diagrams, and textbook pages, and gives feedback on the steps, not just the final answer.
Ideas: snap a photo of handwritten math and get step-by-step feedback · grade a stack of scanned worksheets and group the common mistakes · turn a picture-book or textbook page into an interactive lesson · understand a student's science diagram or lab sketch
🎥 Track 3 · Video & Classroom Understanding
Video holds a lot of what happens in teaching and learning. Turn lectures, demonstrations, and classroom moments into feedback for students and teachers.
Ideas: turn a lecture video into chapters, a study guide, and a quiz · give teachers feedback on talk time and questioning from a classroom recording · watch a student's experiment or presentation and coach them on it · a video explainer that adapts to what the learner already knows
📡 Track 4 · Real-Time Multi-Modal Tutors & Agents
Tutors that work live, like sitting next to a great teacher. Combine live video, voice, and screen or camera input so the AI sees what the student is doing and helps in the moment.
Ideas: a tutor on a live video call that watches a student work a problem and nudges at the right time · a screen-aware coding or homework coach · a phone-camera lab assistant for hands-on science · an AR or camera guide that teaches by pointing at real objects
📖 Track 5 · Multi-Modal Storytelling
Stories are how kids learn to read, imagine, and remember. Build AI that blends voice, images, and video into stories that teach, react to the reader, and let kids create their own.
Ideas: turn a child's drawing and voice recording into an illustrated, narrated story · an interactive read-along that reacts to how the reader is doing · turn a history or science lesson into a narrated illustrated or video story · kids co-creating a story by voice, with images generated as they talk · multilingual narration that reads the same story in a child's home language
🃏 Wildcard (Open Category)
Any multi-modal idea that doesn't fit the tracks above. If it solves a real problem in learning and shows a measurable learning outcome, build it.

Video holds a lot of what happens in teaching and learning. Turn lectures, demonstrations, and classroom moments into feedback for students and teachers.
Ideas: turn a lecture video into chapters, a study guide, and a quiz · give teachers feedback on talk time and questioning from a classroom recording · watch a student's experiment or presentation and coach them on it · a video explainer that adapts to what the learner already knows

Tutors that work live, like sitting next to a great teacher. Combine live video, voice, and screen or camera input so the AI sees what the student is doing and helps in the moment.
Ideas: a tutor on a live video call that watches a student work a problem and nudges at the right time · a screen-aware coding or homework coach · a phone-camera lab assistant for hands-on science · an AR or camera guide that teaches by pointing at real objects
📖 Track 5 · Multi-Modal Storytelling
Stories are how kids learn to read, imagine, and remember. Build AI that blends voice, images, and video into stories that teach, react to the reader, and let kids create their own.
Ideas: turn a child's drawing and voice recording into an illustrated, narrated story · an interactive read-along that reacts to how the reader is doing · turn a history or science lesson into a narrated illustrated or video story · kids co-creating a story by voice, with images generated as they talk · multilingual narration that reads the same story in a child's home language
🃏 Wildcard (Open Category)
Any multi-modal idea that doesn't fit the tracks above. If it solves a real problem in learning and shows a measurable learning outcome, build it.

// HACKDAY FORMAT
⚡ Sprint format — pitch, team up, build, demo, in one day

🛠️ Mentors on hand from the AI Builders community

🏆 Prizes for the most useful, the most ambitious, and the most surprising builds

🍕🍻 Pizza, snacks and drinks throughout

// FOR WHO
✅ Devs, Product peeps, Data lovers, ML engineers, Founders

✅ Anyone building with AI

⚠️ Some LLM knowledge required!*

// AGENDA
09:45 👋 Doors Open
10:00 📋 Welcome & Challenges
10:20 🤝 Pitching & Team Matching
11:00 🚀 Hack Session (+ optional workshop)
12:00 🌯 Lunch (sponsored)
13:00 🚀 Hack Session
17:00 🏆 Demos & Judging
18:30 🔚 End & Optional Dinner
// FAQ
What is AI Builders? A self-organizing nonprofit community of 11000+ AI nerds 🤓. We're building a democratic AI platform, to make our community completely co-owned and co-governed by you (yes, all attendees).

Will it be recorded? Yes, some sessions are streamed live and recorded. By attending, you consent to being photographed and filmed. Let us know if you don't want to be on camera.

I'm not technical. Can I come? Yes, but to actually enjoy the meetup we recommend understanding basic LLM concepts: Agents, Embeddings, RAG, MCPs, Inference, Structured Output, Finetuning, APIs, Reinforcement Learning. Not sure what those mean? Ask any chatbot — that's literally what they're for.

Can I get a free ticket? Can I volunteer? Money should never be the reason not to join. If you need a sponsored ticket, or want to help out by arriving 1.5h early to set up, message Luc .

Can I demo, give a talk, or just help out? Message Luc if you want to shine ✨ on stage and grow your network — community demos are 10 minutes, builder demos are 15-20 minutes.

What time does the hackday start? The hackday starts at 10:00 on Thursday, 14 January.

Do I need to form a team in advance? No! We'll have team formation at the beginning. You can also join solo.

What should I bring? Bring your laptop, charger, and any APIs/tools you want to use.

How do I submit my project? Submit via the hackday dashboard. Include a demo video and GitHub link.

// VENUE & SPONSORS
We look forward to hanging out with you!
Thanks to our friends for hosting us in their beautiful space.

About Event

Wednesday we're hosting a Lightning Mesh hack night @ Embassy -- home of the first Lightning Mesh permanent installation. Duke will start with a short primer on how to decentralize anything by engineering out centralized authority, then go into details on how to use the distributed service mesh.
Come & make your project, build DWeb tech together, explore resilient communication patterns, local-first software stacks, and play around with technology.
We plan to integrate LoRA radios into the stack for metadata/telemetry, upgrade our router mesh administration, maybe do some directional antenna work to connect the Lightning Mesh islands. We will see about storing sensitive data locally (like room recordings), and make democratic house decisions over how that data is used (feeding it to local transcription models, what LLMs can be used for analysis, etc). Knowledge of Iroh and/or babeld routing is a plus. All levels of technical proficiency are welcome.
Lightning Mesh is a project begun out of the needs of refugees and political dissidents in oppressive regimes, that became a study in how centralized authority presents single-point-of-failure chokepoints which can be used against people, and how those are baked in even to our networking stacks. Amid a growing sense that connectivity should be a commons, Lightning Mesh is an attempt to engineer a different way, applying the techniques of decentralized and distributed systems to serve actual people, add censorship-resistant communication to off-the-shelf routers, and create a basis for a distributed local-first service mesh not dependent on ISP-granted internet.
